extracted.intended_audience: IP statisticians, policymakers, researchers, and practitioners at IP offices tracking trademark filing and registration statistics
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and measurement rules used in WIPO's trademark statistical tables and charts (how counts are defined, allocated, and presented across regions, income groups, offices and origins). Useful for producing or interpreting trademark statistics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Income group allocation for regional offices
rubrics_metrics.description: Data for the European Union Intellectual Property Office are allocated to the high-income group, because most EU member states are high-income countries. For the same reason, data for the African Regional Intellectual Property Organization and the African Intellectual Property Organization are allocated to the low-income group.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When aggregating by income group, allocate regional office data to the income group that represents the majority of the member states. See the data description section in Additional information for income group classification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Region/income group coverage counts
rubrics_metrics.description: Totals by geographical region are WIPO estimates using data covering 168 IP offices. Each region includes the following number of offices: Africa (34), Asia (48), Europe (42), Latin America and the Caribbean (37), North America (2) and Oceania (5).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report and document the number of offices included in each region and make explicit that world totals are WIPO estimates based on this coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Figure-specific data coverage (non-resident filing data)
rubrics_metrics.description: Figures based on non-resident filing data from 136 IP offices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State the number of offices used for non-resident filing analyses; do not assume full global coverage unless explicitly stated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Figure-specific data coverage (registrations in force totals)
rubrics_metrics.description: World totals are WIPO estimates using data covering 146 IP offices (for registrations in force).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Different figures may use different subsets of offices; always cite the specific offices/coverage used for each metric.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of origin of a trademark application
rubrics_metrics.description: The origin of a trademark application is determined by the residence of the applicant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When attributing filings to origins, use applicant residence; document treatment of regional filings and multi-jurisdiction filings (see equivalent application definition below).

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of regional office filings for origin and equivalent counts
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications filed at regional offices are considered equivalent to multiple applications in the relevant member states and the classes specified in these applications are multiplied accordingly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For equivalent counts, multiply classes in regional filings by the number of member states covered (or follow the glossary definition). For absolute-origin counts, an application at a regional office may be considered resident if the applicant is resident of one of the member states.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resident vs non-resident filing classification (resident filing rule at regional offices)
rubrics_metrics.description: An application filed at a regional office is considered a resident filing, if the applicant is a resident of one of the relevant member states.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly apply this rule when separating resident and abroad filings; document exceptions if any.

rubrics_metrics.name: Absolute counts vs equivalent counts distinction
rubrics_metrics.description: This figure distinguishes between absolute counts and equivalent counts for filing activity abroad; that is, resident applications are excluded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be clear whether a reported value is an absolute count (raw filings) or an equivalent count (regional filings multiplied to reflect member-state coverage). Provide the equivalent/absolute count ratio where helpful.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of absolute counts vs equivalent counts in origin/office tables
rubrics_metrics.description: The office and origin data shown consist of absolute application class counts rather than equivalent application class counts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State which tables use absolute counts and which use equivalent counts; do not mix without clear labeling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Not adjusting for single-class vs multi-class filing systems
rubrics_metrics.description: Data are based on the numbers of applications filed; that is, differences between single-class and multi-class filing systems across IP offices are not taken into account.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Caution readers that cross-office comparisons may be affected by differing class-filing systems; if adjustment is required, document the method separately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trademark filing activity by origin – absolute-count basis
rubrics_metrics.description: In this figure, trademark application filing activity by origin includes the number of classes specified in resident applications and in applications filed abroad and is based on absolute count, not equivalent count.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When presenting filing activity by origin, explicitly state whether counts are absolute or equivalent and whether resident and abroad classes are both included.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contribution decomposition of total growth (resident vs non-resident)
rubrics_metrics.description: This figure shows the total growth or decrease in application class counts for each office, broken down by the respective contribution made by resident and non-resident filing activity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report total growth rate (%) and decompose it into percentage-point contributions from resident and non-resident filings; include worked examples (e.g., Viet Nam example provided) to illustrate calculation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equivalent/absolute count ratio reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Equivalent/absolute count ratio is reported for filing activity abroad (illustrating the multiplier effect of regional offices like EUIPO).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide the ratio to help interpret how much regional filings inflate equivalent counts; explain causes such as frequent use of regional offices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nice Classification goods vs services split
rubrics_metrics.description: In the 45-class Nice Classification, the first 34 classes indicate goods and the remaining 11 refer to services.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When aggregating by goods/services, use the Nice class boundaries and cite www.wipo.int/classifications/nice for the complete list.

rubrics_metrics.name: Top Nice classes and class-share reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Distribution of non-resident trademark applications by top Nice classes (ranked list with class share %).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify and label abbreviated class descriptions and refer readers to the full Nice class definitions; indicate number of offices used for the sample (e.g., 136 IP offices).

rubrics_metrics.name: Industry sector mapping from Nice classes
rubrics_metrics.description: Industry sectors based on class groups are those defined by Edital (see annex B for full definitions and the composition of Nice goods and services classes).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When presenting sectoral shares, document the mapping from Nice classes to industry sectors and include the annex or mapping table.

rubrics_metrics.name: Registration vs class-count distinction for registrations in force
rubrics_metrics.description: Data refer to the number of trademark registrations in force, not the number of classes specified in those registrations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarify whether metrics count registrations or classes; note that registrations can be maintained indefinitely by paying renewals, affecting in-force totals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Calculation of percent of registrations in force from a registration year
rubrics_metrics.description: Percentages are calculated as follows: the number of trademark registrations issued in year t and in force in 2019 divided by the total number of trademark registrations issued in year t.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this formula to produce time-series survivorship measures; document office coverage (example: based on ~15.8 million active registrations reported by 77 offices).

rubrics_metrics.name: Average age of trademarks in force
rubrics_metrics.description: Average age of trademarks in force reported for selected offices (e.g., values for 2014 and 2019).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compute average age across registrations in force at a given reporting date; document any office-specific coverage issues (e.g., ARIPO, EUIPO notes).

rubrics_metrics.name: Categorization of examination outcomes
rubrics_metrics.description: Distribution categories for trademark examination outcomes: REGISTERED, TOTAL REJECTION, WITHDRAWN/ABANDONED.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When reporting outcomes, use these mutually exclusive categories and state the office sample used for the distribution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Note on year-to-year registration fluctuation due to office resources
rubrics_metrics.description: On the basis of an examination, a registration may be issued for a trademark application. The number of registrations issued may fluctuate greatly from one year to the next, in part reflecting the amount of resources that IP offices dedicate to examining trademark applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interpret large year-to-year changes in registrations with caution; consider office process capacity and policy changes as explanatory factors.
